title: Introduction to MOSCATELLI’s tone of voice
summary: A practical introduction to restraint, clarity and authority in internal and external MOSCATELLI writing.
contentNotice: Demonstration content for Atlas interface development; not final MOSCATELLI policy.

blocks.text: Prefer precise language, calm confidence and useful context. Avoid inflated claims, filler and unnecessary informality.

items: Say exactly what is known and what is not.
Preserve warmth without becoming casual or verbose.

blocks.text: MOSCATELLI should not need to insist that something is exceptional. The writing should communicate confidence through specificity, proportion and control.

blocks.label: Avoid
blocks.text: Generic luxury language such as “unparalleled”, “timeless elegance” or “the finest” should not substitute for concrete information.
Internal communication can be more direct than public copy, but it should remain clear enough that another person can understand the decision, action and context later.

steps.title: Lead with the point
steps.text: State the decision, request or change early.

steps.title: Add material context
steps.text: Include only the information needed to understand why it matters.

steps.title: Make ownership explicit
steps.text: When action is required, identify who owns it and when it is expected.

items: Could the sentence be shorter without losing meaning?
Does the tone sound composed rather than promotional?
Would the wording still make sense outside the immediate conversation?
